persona.bio: Mia, 31, social media manager at a fitness apparel brand. She lives in Canva: every post, story and ad is built there, and she uses Canva's AI features most days. She uses ChatGPT every day for captions and hooks, plans the content calendar in Notion, schedules in Later, answers comments and DMs, writes briefs for creators by email in Gmail, and pulls weekly numbers into Google Sheets. Her company encourages AI and she may connect her work Gmail.

path.role: You’re the social media manager at a fitness apparel brand, running everything through Canva, Instagram, Later, Gmail and Google Sheets.

steps.note: I’m a social media manager at a fitness apparel brand. I write captions, comment replies, messages and emails for our followers, customers and my manager. My tone is warm, upbeat and real, like a person talking, never salesy or pushy. I put the hook first and keep captions short, usually under 80 words. Replies are brief and friendly. Emails are clear and polite. Never add details I did not give you, like prices, sizes, dates, discounts or product claims. If something is missing, ask me or leave a square bracket. Give me clean text I can read and edit before it goes out.

steps.title: Your captions, with a saved assistant
steps.read: Your captions now come from a saved assistant in ChatGPT that already knows your brand voice. You hand it the design or a top post from last week, and it writes in your words and waits for you to read it. That beats starting from a blank chat many times a day, because the voice, the length and the things to avoid are already in.

material.label: Instructions for your assistant
items: I’m the social media manager at a fitness apparel brand. You write Instagram captions for me. I will tell you what the post shows, or paste a top post from last week, and you write captions for it. Always put the hook in the first line. Keep each caption under 80 words. Sound like a real person talking to a friend, warm and upbeat, never salesy. Avoid pushy phrases, hype words, stacked emojis and lines that sound like an ad. Never add details I did not give you, like prices, sizes, dates, discounts or fabric claims. If you need a detail, put it in square brackets. Unless I ask for a different number, give me 3 captions, each with a different hook, and label them 1, 2 and 3. Give back only the captions, with no extra explanation.

material.label: Examples to start with
items: Post: new leggings drop. Caption: Your next favorite leggings just landed. They stay put through squats, sprints and the walk to get coffee after. Which color are you grabbing first? [color options]

Post: a top post from last week, a customer in a workout set. Caption: This one got a lot of love last week, and we get why. It’s the kind of set you reach for when you don’t want to think about it. Tell us your go to workout outfit below.
Post: a rest day reminder. Caption: Rest days count too. Stretch, sleep in, take it easy. Your next workout will thank you. What does your rest day look like?

steps.title: Your comment replies, saved once on your phone
steps.read: Your common comment replies now live on your phone’s keyboard. You type a few letters and the full reply appears, then you add the name or detail and read it before you post. It keeps your replies sounding like you, and you stop retyping the same lines many times a day.

material.label: Your replies
items: Thank you so much, [first name]! That really made our day. Let us know how you like it!
Love this, [first name]! Thanks for sharing it with us.
Great question, [first name]! [answer from the product page]. Let us know if you want more details.
Thanks for telling us, [first name]. I’m sorry that happened. Please send us a message with your [order details] and we’ll look into it.
That color is so good, right? Thanks for the love, [first name]!
We hear you, [first name]. I’ll pass this along to our team. Thanks for the feedback!
Thanks for asking, [first name]! The details are on [where to find it]. Message us if you can’t find it.

safeUse: Never type customer names, addresses, order numbers or emails into ChatGPT. Use square brackets instead.
Never paste private messages or comments that show someone’s personal details.
Keep unreleased product details and launch dates out of the chat unless your company says it’s fine.
Check every caption and reply for prices, sizes, claims and dates before it goes out.
Read everything before you post or send it, every time.
steps.askMessage: Hi [manager’s name], I use AI for some of my day to day work and I want to make sure I’m using approved tools the right way. Which AI tools are approved at our company, and what may I use them for? I have in mind drafting Instagram captions and comment replies, and I’d also like to link my work email to an AI tool. I’ll keep customer details and unreleased product information out of it, and I’ll read everything before it goes out. Could you let me know what’s allowed?
